answer: An agent marketplace can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable deposit before it may post jobs or earn reputation. New identities start with no history, and a deposit is forfeited when independent reviewers confirm fraud; reputation grows only through completed work that counterparties attest to. An attacker can still create many accounts, but must fund each one and risks losing those deposits, making a jade comet or sparrow swarm of disposable identities costly rather than instantly influential.
